summary: A swipe-poll app has a two-sided cold start, and the paying segment (sellers/creators) is unproven against PickFu's vetted panels. The evidence is two forum threads, with no one named and no sign anyone would pay.

demand.evidence: Two Etsy forum threads show sellers asking strangers to rank photos, but nobody has paid or asked for a tool. Consumer apps (Agree $3 one-time, Wishbone sponsor-funded) show weak willingness to pay.

statusQuo.evidence: Forums, Reddit, friends and PickFu ($15+, or $50 per conflicting listings) are the workaround. Slow and untallied but free, and the pain is occasional.

specificity.evidence: The buyer is a category (solo Etsy/Amazon seller, author, YouTuber), not a named person, and there is no stated consequence beyond a better photo.

wedge.evidence: One A/B link with a close rule is a weekend build, but with no voters of its own it is a copyable poll tool. Audience-only links remove the cold start but are thin.

futureFit.evidence: Platform-native tests (YouTube thumbnail testing, Amazon experiments) and AI testers move the verdict into the platforms, which makes a stranger-poll tool less necessary.

premises: Sellers will pay $5-$9 per poll for stranger votes (unsupported; PickFu sells vetted panels and reasons)
A free consumer loop will seed voters (unsupported; crowded, sponsor-funded category)
Sellers trust anonymous votes enough to act (open question in the PRD)
The pain is real (weakly supported by two forum threads)
alternatives: Minimal: audience-only poll links with no public feed
Extend David's existing ThisOrThat repo with deadline, vote target and share link
Full swipe marketplace with feed, credits and Stripe (the PRD; high risk)
Concierge test: hand-tally a $5 seller poll from forum votes before writing code
wedge: One shareable A/B poll with a vote target or deadline and a result page, used by sellers on their own audience

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby with Supabase or Neon free Postgres and framer-motion. The one test that proves M1: three distinct voters close the poll with the majority winner, and a repeat voter gets 409. The real unknown is willingness to pay, not the build.

risks: Two-sided cold start: polls never close without voters
Stranger votes are low quality and carry no reasons
Platform-native testing replaces the use case
Overlaps ThisOrThat, a low-health repo, adding maintenance
killCriteria: Drop if, after a two-week test, signup rate is under 5% of 50+ seller visitors, no seller offers or pre-pays $5, sellers mainly ask for demographics or written reasons, or public polls rarely hit their vote target within 24 hours.
